$comment: Machine-readable design rules. NEVER read by a model — executed by the pre-present checker (scripts/design-check/). Prose principles live in references/design-doctrine.md; scoring lives in data/design-rubric.md. Each rule's `status` is the honest build state: 'pending' = specified but no implementation exists yet, so it enforces NOTHING.

meta.rebaseline_reason: F2 rule 30 (escape treadmill): today's escape becomes tomorrow's tell. The cliche catalogue below rots. Re-check the F2 source and community baseline roughly quarterly.

tiers.block_feasibility: The variant cannot run in the target sandbox AT ALL — eval, WebAssembly, any network reference, inline on* handlers, or an ungated non-Widely feature carrying layout/legibility. Violation = regenerate, never presented. Fail closed. NEVER varies by audience profile, because a blank panel is blank for everyone. Added 2026-07-23 from H2 + E2; extends the owner's two-tier ruling (which governs QUALITY) rather than revising it (this governs EXISTENCE). Flagged for owner confirmation.
tiers.block_owner: Owner's own constraints + the isolation gate. Violation = regenerate, never presented. Fail closed. NEVER varies by audience profile.
tiers.block_floor: The hard doctrine gates. Violation = regenerate. Deliberately tiny, and FILTERED BY AUDIENCE PROFILE (see audience_profiles).
tiers.advise: Computed, annotated on the variant, shown. A Rebuild band triggers ONE auto-regeneration, then shows with the score visible.

meta.measurement_note: C2 §3.10 CHANGES HOW THE CHECKER MUST WORK: coherence and token-adherence rules are RUNTIME checks (render, then getComputedStyle), not source-text greps. A source grep cannot see cascade resolution, so it cannot tell whether the same semantic role resolves to the same value across two components. Rules below carry `method`: 'source' (static grep over the variant text) or 'computed' (needs a browser). The block_feasibility rules are all 'source', which is why they are the cheapest to implement first.
meta.owner_override: An explicit owner instruction outranks every tier (doctrine rule 22: an explicit request IS a decision). Overridden rules are recorded in the ledger with rationale and exempted from the templated tax.

audience_profiles.$comment: Owner ruling 2026-07-23: a rule is not universally true, it is true for an audience on a device. Research states rules against an implied general-public/all-devices reader; most of this owner's projects are not that. The project's profile is a first-class REVISABLE ledger field and it selects which floor rules bind. block_owner rules NEVER vary by profile.
audience_profiles.graduation: A profile may change (personal tool goes public). Every decision records the profile its rationale depended on, so a profile change automatically re-opens exactly those decisions instead of leaving silent debt. This is the whole reason the rationale must name the profile.

P1.name: solo
P1.typical: 1 user (the owner), built by them, single large display, mouse + keyboard
P1.example: a personal dashboard on a 27-inch monitor
P1.responsive_range: primary display only (4K-first if that is the primary screen)

P2.name: trusted-group
P2.typical: a handful of known users (family/friends), built by the owner, laptop-class displays
P2.example: a shared media library used by 7 people on laptops
P2.flag_note: some laptops are touchscreens — flag hover-only content, do not block it
P2.screen_reader: skip unless a member needs it — ASK ONCE at the context gate, then record

P3.name: public
P3.typical: unknown users, all devices, mobile through monitor
P3.example: a public blog or stats site

audience_profiles.invariant: The isolation gate (iso-*), the owner's constraint contract, and 'never show one option' apply at EVERY profile — they protect the integrity of the decision, not the audience.

worked_instance.decision: card keeps title, rating and Play in a hover-revealed footer
worked_instance.verdict: accepted informed trade-off; under P3 this would be a blocking B2 §3.5 defect

hover_only_content.statement: Content or actions revealed ONLY on :hover are invisible to touch, keyboard and pen users. Hover is polish; the underlying affordance must be persistent.
hover_only_content.detectors: an element whose visibility/transform/opacity is driven solely by a :hover selector and that contains a link, button, or the component's primary label

constraint_contract_schema.$comment: The owner's per-project contract, stored in the ledger and injected into EVERY round. These are tier block_owner.

must_use.semantics: Every listed master_components id must appear in the variant source, tagged.

animation_vocab.semantics: Parse every @keyframes name, animation-name, and transition-property in the variant. ONLY the listed vocabulary may appear. Anything outside fails.

detectors.glassmorphism: backdrop-filter present, or filter:blur() on a translucent surface
detectors.parallax: scroll listener altering transform, or background-attachment:fixed, or animation-timeline:scroll()
detectors.bounce: cubic-bezier with an overshoot control point (y<0 or y>1), or easing named bounce/elastic/back
detectors.glow: box-shadow or filter:drop-shadow with a saturated colour and no offset

source_policy.semantics: library-first (DEFAULT, owner ruling 2026-07-23) = check master_components first, use a catalog entry where it genuinely fits, author bespoke freely when it does not; every variant must declare source as an mc-id or 'bespoke'. library-only = every component traces to an mc-id. bespoke-ok = no constraint, tagging still required.
source_policy.enforced_by: catalog-source.mjs checkSourcePolicy, wired into build-variant-set.mjs; stage3-gates.test.mjs (7 cases incl. 3 must-fail). C2 2026-07-27: the missing tagging convention now exists - variant.source = {kind:"catalog", mc_id} | {kind:"bespoke", why}.

colour_budget.semantics: Count distinct rendered surfaces carrying the derived accent. Over budget = fail. Under-use is NOT a pass: a fully monochrome result fails the 'restraint is not monochrome' half of the rule.
colour_budget.enforced_by: computed-checks.js colourBudget; surfaced as a BLOCK by computed-runner.mjs blockingFindings. C4 2026-07-27. Monochrome is REPORTED, not blocked - a deliberately monochrome design is a legitimate owner choice.

rules.statement: The named axis parameter provably differs across every pair in the set.
rules.params_note: 0.15 is a [REASONED] engineering default, not a measured constant (G1 §8). Tune per axis against real 'felt identical' reports.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/preview-build/isolation-gate.test.mjs › "felt identical" set is REJECTED › axis-diff catches it

rules.statement: Every non-axis variable is token-identical across all variants in the set.
rules.note: This is the check that makes a lock TRUE rather than a guess about why the owner picked.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/preview-build/isolation-gate.test.mjs › contaminated set is REJECTED › control-diff catches the second axis

rules.statement: Each variant's level on the named axis is stateable without ambiguity.
rules.note: If the tool cannot articulate where each variant sits, a human never will and the set will feel identical.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/preview-build/isolation-gate.test.mjs › good set passes the gate › blind-sort ok

rules.statement: Option count fits the rung: 3 default; 2 for binary axis or late confirm; 4-5 only at rung 0-1 on a foundational axis; never 6+; never 1.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/preview-build/isolation-gate.test.mjs › 6 options is REJECTED even at rung 0 / 3 options at rung 4 (page) is REJECTED

rules.statement: Never present a single option for approval.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/preview-build/isolation-gate.test.mjs › a single option is REJECTED

rules.statement: Before locking an axis, every parent axis it depends on is already locked.
rules.params_note: [REASONED]. The RULE (parents before children) is invariant; this specific order is a default a brand-led product may legitimately reorder.

rules.statement: After any regeneration, every previously-locked target is identical to its stored snapshot. Any drift is reverted and flagged.
rules.note: Treat locks as golden files under test. Requires a snapshot per locked target in the ledger.

rules.statement: Slot order is randomised on every presentation, not just the first.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/preview-build/harness-dsd.test.mjs › shuffle randomises slot order, reproducible per seed, lossless

rules.statement: Variants are labelled A/B/C or by number. No evaluative adjectives, no 'recommended' marker, no pre-selection.
rules.note: Suspends the skill's usual 'put the recommended option first' house style — for TASTE choices only.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/preview-build/isolation-gate.test.mjs › evaluative labels are REJECTED

rules.source: CHATGPT (WCAG 2.1 AA) + A5 pending; F2 §3.12 wants APCA
rules.statement: Text contrast >= 4.5:1 normal, >= 3:1 large (>=18.66px bold or >=24px). Non-text UI >= 3:1 against adjacent colour.

advisory_companion.note: APCA is DRAFT with an unconfirmed embedding licence — computed and shown, never gates. Revisit if it lands in WCAG 3.

rules.impl_note: computed-checks.js: resolved text colour vs the nearest opaque ancestor background → WCAG ratio. Text over an image/gradient is reported 'review', never silently passed. Profile-filtered (advise P1, block P2/P3).
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/computed-checks.test.mjs (math) + computed-checks.browser.test.mjs › CATCH: low contrast is flagged (DOM, real Chromium)

rules.statement: Any variant carrying motion declares @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and neutralises non-essential animation within it.
Interactive targets are >= 24x24 CSS px.
No state or meaning is carried by colour alone — every coloured status cue has a second channel (icon, label, shape, weight).
rules.note: Also the method's own 'state reads via form, not only colour' rule.

rules.statement: No more than 3 flashes per second.
Visible focus indicator: >=2px thick, >=3:1 against BOTH the component and the surface behind it, drawn with outline + outline-offset (NOT box-shadow alone), via :focus-visible.
rules.why_not_box_shadow: forced-colors: active deletes box-shadow entirely, so a box-shadow-only ring vanishes for Windows High Contrast users.

rules.source: B1 §3.1-3.3 (the authoritative ladder; supersedes the ChatGPT 200-500ms approximation)
rules.statement: Duration by ROLE, not one range. Exits run 20-30% shorter than entrances. Duration scales with distance/size (+50-100ms per size step).

Enter decelerates (ease-out), exit accelerates (ease-in), move-within-view is symmetric. NEVER linear for positional motion — linear is only for continuous motion (spinners, marquees, real progress) and opacity cross-fades.
Animate only transform and opacity. width/height/top/left/margin/padding trigger layout; box-shadow/filter/background/color/border-radius trigger paint. Frame budget ~10ms at 60Hz.
Stagger 20-60ms per item; cap the total sequence at 300-500ms. Past ~8-10 items animate only what is in the viewport.
Motion must never sit un-mitigated behind reading text. Visible movement behind text at rest is a defect. Auto-motion lasting >5s alongside content needs a pause control.
Saturated accent covers ~10% of pixels: ~60% dominant neutral, ~30% secondary surface/text, ~10% accent earned by a RANKED list of surfaces. Accent everywhere reads cheap; accent nowhere reads dead.
rules.note: The numeric form of the owner's colour-budget rule. Both must pass — this counts pixels, colour_budget counts surfaces.

rules.statement: One accent hue family; the four semantic colours (success/warn/danger/info) are a SEPARATE axis. Never derive danger-red or success-green from the accent. If a derived accent lands on a semantic hue, nudge one apart.

Never pure black in dark mode — base surface at OKLCH L ~= 0.18 (#121212). Elevation on dark is +lightness (~+0.03 L per step), not shadow. Cut accent chroma 10-30% on dark; avoid pure-white text (L ~= 0.90 / #E6E6E6).
Neutrals are hue-tinted, never pure grey, but leashed: OKLCH chroma 0.004-0.02. Below reads as flat computer-grey; above ~0.03 the greys visibly turn blue/beige.
State deltas are direction-aware lightness moves, not a second hardcoded hex. Hover ~= dL +/-0.04-0.06, press ~= +/-0.08-0.10, so one rule darkens in light and lightens in dark.

Derive content colour by ROLE (vibrant swatch, not most-common pixel), then normalise L to the theme's accent target and clamp C so contrast is guaranteed AT DERIVATION TIME. Never paint a surface with the raw extracted pick.
rules.implementation_note: theme-extract.mjs already picks vibrant-not-dominant and skips near-black/near-grey. The L-normalise + C-clamp step is the outstanding upgrade.

rules.statement: Body measure 45-75ch, 65 default, hard outer bound 80 (40 for CJK) — REGARDLESS of viewport, including on a 3840px panel. Route extra width to a second pane, never a longer line.

On large displays add STRUCTURE, not width: one stacked pane -> 50/50 -> 70/30, never one stretched column. And a 27-inch 4K panel is NOT 3840 CSS px — OSes default it to ~150% scaling, giving a logical viewport around 2560x1440.
rules.corrects: The method's 'primary-screen-tuned, 4K-first' instruction assumed the marketing resolution.

rules.statement: Data-dense surfaces get their own 4px density scale, decoupled from the 8pt layout grid, once a grid shows >15-20 rows. Row heights: comfortable 48-64, standard 40, compact 32, extra-compact 24. Under ~32px needs a target-size review.
Z-index is a tiered token ladder with gaps >=100, never a raw integer and never 9999. For anything that must always win, prefer the browser top layer (<dialog>, [popover]).
Whitespace is the FIRST hierarchy tool. A section heading carries 1.5-2x more space above than below — that asymmetry says 'this heading belongs to what follows' at zero colour cost.
Body text >= ~14-16px equivalent with 1.4-1.6x line-height.
Spacing values fall on one declared scale; no more than ~6-8 distinct values on a screen; every value a multiple of the base unit.
rules.params_note: C2 §3.10 supplies the tolerance the G2 statement lacked: a computed value is 'on-ramp' if it is within ±0.5-1px of a ramp entry. Sub-pixel drift from percentage/flex layout is expected and must not be reported as scale debt.

rules.statement: No more than ~5-7 distinct font-size steps, all from the declared scale.

rules.source: G2 §4.6 dim 2, tolerance + method from C2 §3.10
rules.statement: Every colour value traces to the declared token set — no one-off hex outside it.
rules.params_note: C2 §3.10 supplies the tolerance the G2 statement lacked. ΔE2000 <=1 pass, <=2 warn, >2 fail. Compare the COMPUTED colour against the resolved token value, not the source text — a source grep cannot see cascade resolution or color-mix()/oklch() output.

rules.statement: Tokens flow primitive -> semantic -> component and never skip or reverse a layer; primitives are named by value, semantics by role, components by part; alias depth <= 3 hops.
rules.params_note: Detectable statically: parse every `--x: var(--y)` edge into a graph. Defects = a component token referencing a primitive directly, a cycle, a chain > 3, a primitive whose name carries a role word (primary/action/danger/surface), or a semantic whose name carries a colour word (blue/red/grey).
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-token-layer-direction flags a name mixing colour + role, and a too-deep chain

rules.statement: No component holds a raw literal that duplicates an existing token value.
rules.params_note: A literal `border-radius: 8px` sitting next to `--radius-2: 8px` is drift-in-waiting. Flag every literal length/colour/duration whose value equals a declared token's value. Exempt: 0, 1px hairlines, 100%/auto, and values inside the token declarations themselves.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-raw-value-drift flags a literal that duplicates a token value

rules.statement: The same semantic role resolves to the same computed value across every component, and every component maps the shared state vocabulary to the same token delta.
rules.params_note: THE MIX-COHERENCE CHECK G1 REQUIRES. Makes a per-item mixed pick (doctrine 38) safe: when the owner takes the header from v1 and the card from v2, this proves the result is still one design. BUILT in computed-checks.js: groups [data-role] elements, getComputedStyle, ΔE across components. Requires the generation method to stamp data-role on role-bearing parts (a small addition). Runs in real Chromium.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/computed-checks.test.mjs (ΔE math) + computed-checks.browser.test.mjs › CATCH: cross-component coherence flags the drifting role

rules.source: G1 §4.3 (rendered), added 2026-07-23 from the round-1 false-reject
rules.statement: Across the N rendered panels, each pair's RESOLVED-style signature differs by at least a floor — the panels actually look different, not just differ in source.
rules.params_note: THE PROPER BACKSTOP FOR A STYLISTIC BUNDLE. The gate's source structural check counts tag/class/property NAMES and is BLIND to CSS-value differences, so it reported ~2% for three visibly-different round-1 cards (a false reject). This reads getComputedStyle, so it sees radius 0 vs 14, flat vs shadowed, coral vs amber. Per panel: the SET of resolved values across all styled elements (a holistic look signature); distance = mean Jaccard across props. Advise, not block, because it complements — not replaces — the source gate. Verified on real round-2 output: A/B 0.39, A/C 0.41, B/C 0.57 (all differ); a near-identical pair scored 0.06 (flagged).
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/computed-checks.test.mjs (vecDistance) + computed-checks.browser.test.mjs › CATCH: divergence flags near-identical panels + PASS: different panels diverge

rules.statement: The variant source contains no eval, new Function, string-argument setTimeout/setInterval, or javascript: URI.
rules.params_note: Applies to INLINED LIBRARY SOURCE too, not just hand-written code — H2 §3.15: verify the pinned version's actual text, because popular libraries have shipped eval in avoidable paths (Chart.js pre-v3 string templates).
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › feas-no-eval fires on dynamic code and not on clean source

rules.statement: No WebAssembly. 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is a SEPARATE CSP keyword from 'unsafe-eval' and is not granted, so WebAssembly.instantiate/compile refuse in every engine.
rules.params_note: Rive's web runtime is UNAVAILABLE, always — not conditionally. Lottie (lottie-web, MIT) is plain JS with no eval and DOES work inlined; prefer SVG+CSS/WAAPI first.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › feas-no-wasm fires on WebAssembly and on Rive by name

rules.statement: The variant makes no network reference of any kind: no external src/href, no @import of a remote URL, no fetch/XHR/WebSocket/EventSource, no remote webfont.
rules.params_note: 'Single-file' and 'no-network' are TWO SEPARATE CHECKS (H2 §3.10) — a technique can be trivially single-file and still fetch at runtime. Tailwind must be compiled to a static stylesheet OFFLINE; the Play CDN is a runtime network call and fails here. known_placeholder_services (D2 §3.9) is called out separately because it is the SPECIFIC failure a generator produces when art is missing: reach for placehold.co or DiceBear's HTTP API. The correct answer is a deterministic seeded inline SVG (doctrine 153) or an initials avatar at the L=0.179 crossover (doctrine 154) — both offline and both stable across rebuilds, which a remote service is not.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › feas-no-network fires on remote refs AND on placeholder services

rules.statement: No inline event-handler attributes (onclick=, onload=, ...). Wire every listener through addEventListener inside the one covered <script> block.
rules.params_note: A hash/nonce-based strict script-src does not cover onclick= by default — only 'unsafe-inline' or the narrower 'unsafe-hashes' does. Separately (E2 §3.7) inline style="" attributes are governed by style-src-attr and are dropped under a hash-based policy; that is adv-inline-style-attr, not this rule.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › feas-no-inline-handlers fires on on* attributes only in markup

rules.statement: Any feature below Baseline Widely Available that carries layout or legibility is @supports-gated with the fallback declared FIRST, outside the gate.
rules.params_note: E2 §3.3: for COLOUR VALUES the cascade is itself the fallback (`color:#a33; color:oklch(...)`) so no @supports is required — hence cascade_fallback_exempt. The gate applies to PROPERTIES that change layout or need a companion rule. Content must remain complete and usable when a gated feature no-ops.

rules.statement: Every degradation ladder has a true bottom rung: zero JS, zero gated CSS feature, always renders correctly. That rung is what ships under prefers-reduced-motion, to any engine failing a feature check, and to anything that throws.
rules.params_note: HARDEST RULE IN THE SET TO AUTOMATE and honestly flagged as such. A credible approximation: render the variant twice with JS disabled and with prefers-reduced-motion:reduce forced, and assert the accessible text content and the primary layout box are unchanged. Do NOT claim this is enforced until that harness exists.

rules.statement: Any canvas/WebGL surface carrying information (not pure decoration) has that information mirrored in real DOM text.
rules.params_note: Canvas and WebGL expose NO accessibility semantics. The mirror is cheap (a visually-hidden table or summary) relative to rebuilding the visual in SVG, and it is the only way the content exists for a screen reader. Advise rather than block because 'is it decorative?' is not mechanically decidable; at P3 with screen-reader support on, this should be promoted to block_floor.

rules.statement: No -webkit-font-smoothing / -moz-osx-font-smoothing.
rules.params_note: Non-standard and macOS-only: a no-op on Windows/Android, but on Mac it forces grayscale AA that renders text lighter, so a design tuned on Windows looks different on Mac. Text is heavier on Windows (DirectWrite) and lighter on macOS (CoreText) by default; design for both. Found in and removed from both of our own preview templates 2026-07-23.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-no-font-smoothing fires on the property but NOT on a comment mentioning it

rules.statement: backdrop-filter is preceded by -webkit-backdrop-filter; mask/mask-composite is preceded by -webkit-mask-* using the WebKit keywords (source-over/source-in, not add/intersect).
rules.params_note: Safari < 18 needs the backdrop-filter prefix. The mask keywords genuinely DIFFER between prefixed and standard — copying the standard keyword into the prefixed line is a silent no-op. The map is per-operation: E2 §3.9 supplied add/intersect, A4 §3.12 supplied exclude->xor (the one the gradient-border trick actually needs). Neither track states the full map; it came from cross-checking them.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-webkit-prefix-pair fires on a missing prefix and a mis-copied keyword

rules.statement: Prefer one <style> block plus classes over inline style="" attributes.
rules.params_note: Governed by style-src-attr, SEPARATELY from style-src; under a strict hash-based policy inline style attributes are dropped and the page silently un-styles. AI-generated markup leans on them heavily, which is exactly why this is worth counting. ADVISE not block, because our observed Artifact sandbox does allow them (see the doctrine's arbitrated-conflicts register) — the risk is portability, not current breakage. Exempt: a style attribute carrying only a CSS custom property used as a per-instance parameter.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-inline-style-attr fires on real declarations but exempts custom-property-only

rules.statement: No meaning (state, contrast, category) depends on wide-gamut P3 saturation; P3 is declared after an sRGB value so the cascade degrades it.
rules.params_note: P3 only SHOWS on a P3 display and is gamut-mapped elsewhere, so extra saturation can never be the carrier of meaning. Pairs with floor-not-colour-alone.

rules.statement: When N variants share one document, no two may declare the same SVG id, CSS class, @keyframes name, or :root custom property.
rules.params_note: DOWNGRADED block_owner -> advise 2026-07-23: markup panels now render in isolated declarative shadow roots (commit 4813ffa), so a cross-variant id/class/keyframes/:root collision is HARMLESS — url(#id) resolves within the panel’s own shadow root. Kept as an advisory because namespacing is still good hygiene; blocking would reject legitimate isolated sets. Historical rationale: url(#id) and <use href="#id"> resolve to the FIRST match in document order, and a later <style> block wins for equal specificity, so variant B silently renders with variant A's gradient/filter/rules. The gate then passes a set whose SOURCE differs while the DISPLAY is identical — which is precisely the failure the gate exists to prevent. Only applies to the harness's markup mode (variant.panelTemplate); token mode is structurally immune because it varies only inline custom properties. See the register's defect entry for the three candidate fixes.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › block-svg-id-collision still DETECTS shared ids/classes/keyframes/:root, now as advisory

rules.statement: Radii come from one role ladder; at most two unrelated radius families (a tight and a loose) appear on a screen.
rules.params_note: Also flag a radius >= ~40% of the element's smaller dimension on elements under 16px (A4 §3.3: a 12px radius on a 16px chip eats the chip), and any non-zero radius on a full-bleed edge-touching element (leaves a sliver).

rules.statement: A rounded element inside a rounded container uses inner = max(0, outer - gap), not the outer radius.
rules.params_note: Measurable at runtime: for each nested rounded pair, compare the child's computed border-radius against max(0, parentRadius - parentPadding). Off by more than 1px = corners run un-parallel and the gap visibly pinches.

rules.statement: Every shadow on the page shares one light source: horizontal offset ~0, vertical offset positive, and vertical ~2x horizontal where horizontal is non-zero.
rules.params_note: Inset shadows are exempt (they are edge highlights, rule 127, not elevation). As elevation rises, offset and blur must increase together while per-layer opacity falls.

rules.statement: Elevation shadows are multi-layer and tinted toward the surface hue, never a single pure-black blur.
rules.params_note: Pure black (hue-less, chroma 0) reads muddy and dead. In DARK MODE this rule mostly should not fire at all: shadows barely read on a near-black surface, so the correct answer is surface-tint + hairline + optional glow (doctrine 121, corroborating A1 rule 65). If a dark variant leans on cast shadows for elevation, that is the finding.

rules.statement: Text over a backdrop-filtered or translucent surface still meets 4.5:1 (large/UI 3:1); the surface is @supports-gated with an opaque fallback, ships -webkit-backdrop-filter, and honours prefers-reduced-transparency.
rules.params_note: MEASUREMENT CAVEAT, stated honestly: the effective background behind glass is the BLURRED COMPOSITE, which getComputedStyle cannot report. A credible implementation screenshots the region and samples actual pixels behind the text — otherwise this rule can only check that the guard rails (fallback, prefix, reduced-transparency) exist, not that contrast is met. Do not claim the contrast half is enforced until pixel sampling exists.

rules.statement: Any translucent or backdrop-filtered surface has a prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce branch that makes it opaque.
rules.params_note: This is the FOURTH preference query (doctrine 58); A5 listed only three and A4 supplied it. Deliberately filed as advise rather than block_floor: the owner's ruling named exactly four floor rules and expanding a profile-filtered floor is the owner's call, not mine. CANDIDATE FOR PROMOTION to block_floor at P2/P3 alongside floor-reduced-motion — flagged for owner decision.

rules.statement: The focus indicator is outline-based; a box-shadow ring may accompany it but must never be the only focus affordance.
rules.params_note: ARBITRATED CONFLICT, see doctrine §6. A4 §3.13 is right that box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px draws a ring without shifting layout, and it is the better tool for dividers and hairlines. But forced-colors mode deletes box-shadow entirely, leaving a Windows High Contrast user with NO visible focus. A5 is the conformance authority (doctrine 54) and wins for focus specifically. Overlaps floor-focus-ring, which owns the >=2px / >=3:1 geometry; this rule owns the mechanism.

rules.statement: Line-height is set per role: body 1.4-1.6, display 1.05-1.25, small print 1.5-1.7.
rules.params_note: The missing half of adv-line-length, which specified the measure but not the leading. Leading rises with measure and falls with size, so a single global line-height across a 12->48px range is the defect this catches.

rules.statement: At most two font families; a third needs a written reason. Two families from the same class (e.g. two neutral sans) is a defect, not a system.
rules.params_note: A2 §3.3: 'subtle differences look like accidents, clear differences look like design.' Two near-identical neutral sans read as a mistake. Detecting 'same class' from a family name alone is unreliable — flag for human judgement rather than asserting it.

rules.statement: Numerics that are columnar or that update in place use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
rules.params_note: The proportional-lining default makes a live timer or a stat tile JITTER as digits change width — a defect the owner would feel without being able to name it. Detect: numeric text inside a table column, or any element whose textContent changes and matches /^[\d.,:%$-]+$/.

rules.statement: On dark backgrounds type drops ~10-15% in weight (or lowers a GRAD axis) and opens tracking +0.01-0.02em.
rules.params_note: The OPTICAL half of the dark-mode adjustment; A1 rule 66 owns the CHROMATIC half (cut accent chroma, avoid pure white). Light-on-dark blooms, so identical weight and tracking in both modes means one of them is wrong. Prefer a GRAD axis change where the face has one: it re-weights without reflow.

rules.statement: Every font-family stack ends in a generic and has a metric-matched fallback with size-adjust / ascent-override / descent-override so the pre-paint frame does not shift layout.
Inter is not used as an unexamined default.
rules.params_note: An F2 tell in typographic form: Inter is excellent and EVERYWHERE, so reaching for it reflexively costs distinctiveness. Not a prohibition — an explicit owner choice of Inter is a decision (doctrine 22) and exempt. This fires only when no typeface rationale was recorded.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-not-default-inter flags an unexamined default typeface

rules.statement: All icons come from one family, on one grid, at one stroke weight.
rules.params_note: Detect by clustering inline SVG icons on viewBox dimensions and stroke-width. Mixed grids or stroke weights read as visual noise even when nobody can name why — D2 calls this the most common iconography defect.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-single-icon-set flags mixed icon grids/strokes

rules.statement: Icons are delivered as inline SVG with currentColor, never as an icon font or an .
rules.params_note: Distinct from feas-no-network: an icon font embedded as a data: URI passes the network check but is still a11y-hostile and monochrome-only. Advise rather than block because the failure is quality, not rendering.

rules.statement: Missing art is a deterministic seeded inline SVG; initials avatars pick text colour at the L=0.179 luminance crossover.
rules.params_note: The network half is enforced by feas-no-network's known_placeholder_services. This rule owns the positive requirement: same seed => same image forever, so a rebuild does not silently change the design. The 0.179 crossover is the genuinely provable part — choosing black above / white below it floors contrast at ~4.58:1 against ANY solid background, which beats guessing.

rules.statement: Images use a fixed aspect-ratio vocabulary and object-fit: cover with a focal object-position; object-fit: fill never appears.
rules.params_note: Distorted faces and products are an instant credibility hit. Also flag a raw width+height pair that implies a ratio outside the vocabulary.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-no-image-distortion flags object-fit: fill

rules.statement: No brand logo is hand-drawn or approximated; real marks are sourced from a licence-clean set, and trademark obligations are respected independently of the file licence.
rules.params_note: NOT MECHANICALLY DECIDABLE and flagged as such — a checker cannot tell an authentic mark from a good imitation. Implement as a PROMPT-TIME constraint plus a provenance annotation the generator must supply for any recognisable brand mark. The legal point is the one that matters and it is easy to get wrong: Simple Icons' SVG data is CC0, but CC0 waives COPYRIGHT, not TRADEMARK — it does not permit implying endorsement, altering the mark, or ignoring clear-space and approved-colour guidelines.

rules.statement: Any control revealed on :hover is also revealed on :focus-within, and has a >=24x24 hit area.
rules.params_note: DISTINCT FROM hover_only_content, which is the profile-filtered discoverability rule. This is OPERABILITY (WCAG 2.1.1): a control that appears only on :hover is unreachable by anyone who tabbed to the row, INCLUDING the solo owner at P1. Detect: a selector containing :hover that sets display/visibility/opacity on a descendant containing a button/a/input, with no sibling :focus-within rule. The fix is one extra selector, which is why this is advised even at P1 rather than skipped.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-hover-control-focus-within fires when a hover reveal has no keyboard path

rules.statement: Numeric table columns are right-aligned and use tabular figures; text columns are left-aligned.
Bar and column charts start at zero. A line chart may use a non-zero baseline only when it is visually flagged.
rules.params_note: A non-zero bar baseline distorts LENGTH-encoded comparison: C3 cites a 13% real increase reading as a 460% increase. Line charts encode by position/slope, so a non-zero baseline is defensible when zero is arbitrary (temperature) or would hide a critical change — but it must carry an axis-break mark or annotated range, never be silent.

rules.statement: Charts carry at most 5-7 series, prefer direct labels to a legend, and switch to small multiples past ~7.
rules.params_note: Pairs with adv-encoding-channel. A legend costs a memorise-then-cross-reference step; direct labels at the endpoint or peak remove it. The 8-hue cap is the same number A1 rule 69 reached for CVD-safe categorical sets, from a different direction (Munzner: categorical hue distinguishability drops past ~8).

rules.statement: The most important quantitative comparison uses the highest-accuracy perceptual channel available.
rules.params_note: Cleveland & McGill, extended by Mackinlay. Precise numeric comparison -> position or length (bar/dot/line). Rough magnitude or a third dimension -> area (bubble). Category identity, NOT magnitude -> hue. Encoding a precise comparison in area or hue is the finding.

rules.statement: Loading, empty and error look different from each other and from genuinely-zero; and the three empty states (nothing-yet / cleared / no-results) have distinct copy and actions.
rules.params_note: Extends adv-nonhappy-states, which only asked that empty/loading/error EXIST. C3 §3.15 adds that they must be mutually distinguishable — a table that just goes blank reads as broken. D1 §3.7 adds that reusing one generic empty string for create-vs-restore-vs-adjust-filters is a common avoidable failure. One primary CTA only.

rules.statement: Navigation item counts sit in the convention band for their surface, and no desktop sidebar is hidden behind a hamburger.
rules.params_note: HONESTY FLAG: '7+-2' is FOLKLORE for menus — NN/g is explicit that menu size is 'not 7, despite a common myth'. These bands come from observed convention (mobile bottom nav, iOS tab bars, desktop global nav), not from a memory limit, and are soft. What IS measured is the cost of HIDING nav: hamburger-only was used in 27% of desktop sessions vs 48-50% visible, discoverability fell >20%, task difficulty rose 21%, completion was >=39% slower on desktop. Fire hard on a hidden desktop sidebar; fire softly on counts.

rules.statement: At least two redundant location cues are present at all times (page title/H1, nav highlight, breadcrumb, URL).
rules.params_note: A conformance floor, not polish: WCAG 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA). Process-step pages are exempt.

rules.statement: Shareable and restorable state lives in the URL: active tab, filters, sort, selection, query, page, wizard step.

replaceState_for: refining state within the same step

rules.params_note: The pushState/replaceState split is the part that gets missed: using pushState for every filter tweak means Back needs thirty presses to escape a filter session.

rules.statement: Progressive disclosure never exceeds two levels.
rules.params_note: A third disclosure level is a documented usability failure pattern, not a judgement call.

rules.statement: Action labels are verb + object, 2-4 words, sentence case; no bare generic labels where a specific verb-object pair exists.
rules.params_note: One of the cheapest and highest-signal source checks in the whole set: a literal wordlist over button/link text. 'Yes'/'No' are additionally banned as confirmation-dialog labels by D1 §3.8, which wants the verb outcome ('Delete file' / 'Keep file').
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-action-label-specific fires on bare generic labels

rules.statement: Error copy states what happened, why (only if it helps), and how to fix; it never blames the user and never exposes a raw code in the primary message.
rules.params_note: D1 §3.4's split is the part that is usually missed: an EMPTY field needs an instruction ('Enter your first name'), a VIOLATED CONSTRAINT needs a description ('First name must be 35 characters or fewer'). Codes go behind a collapsed 'Show technical details'.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-error-copy-shape fires on blaming vocabulary in visible copy

rules.statement: No implementation vocabulary appears in user-facing copy.
rules.params_note: Highly checkable and a reliable tell. Also covers D1 §3.11's synonym drift in spirit: one concept, one word. Scope to user-visible text nodes and attribute values (aria-label, placeholder, title, alt), NOT to code or class names — otherwise it fires on everything.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-no-implementation-vocabulary scans visible text, not class names

rules.statement: Copy holds plain-language defaults, truncates on a budget, and is written to survive translation.
rules.params_note: The i18n clause is structural, not stylistic, and is the one a generator breaks by default: NEVER assemble a sentence from fragments concatenated around a variable — one full sentence per parameterised string, with real ICU plural categories. A button sized to the English verb will not fit German or Finnish. Never truncate an identifier, price, date or nav label — those are exactly what a user distinguishes items by.

rules.statement: A single-file variant stays within budget: <=1MB snappy, <=2MB acceptable, >2MB is a budget event; no single base64 raster exceeds ~150-200KB encoded.
rules.params_note: Offline there is no 'link it instead' escape, so weight is a hard design input rather than a delivery concern. base64 costs exactly +1/3; over HTTP with Brotli that shrinks to ~2.5-5% on the wire, but from file:// it is paid in full and the decode cost is ALWAYS paid. Encode photographs before embedding (AVIF ~50% smaller than JPEG, WebP 25-35%) — but prefer WebP where decode latency matters, because AVIF decodes slower and can cost INP even with zero network.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-weight-budget fires past the snappy target

rules.statement: CSS is organised with @layer in the order reset -> base -> tokens -> layout -> components -> utilities; no ID selectors and no !important are used for styling.
rules.params_note: A later layer wins REGARDLESS of specificity, which is the mechanism that keeps specificity flat at scale. !important is doubly bad here because it REVERSES layer order. :where() has specificity (0,0,0); :is()/:has()/:not() take their most specific argument. Pairs with C2 rule 89: C2 orders the VALUES (primitive->semantic->component), E1 orders the CASCADE.
rules.enforced_by: scripts/design-check/design-check.test.mjs › adv-css-layer-order fires on !important, ID selectors and a wrong @layer order

rules.statement: Embedded fonts are subset once to the glyphs used and output as WOFF2; a variable font is used only at >=3 weights; the face is not split into multiple unicode-range subsets.
rules.params_note: CORRECTS a naive application of doctrine rule 141: unicode-range and font-display exist to manage per-range lazy download and FOIT/FOUT, and OFFLINE THERE IS NEITHER — splitting a face into many subsets saves nothing and adds parse blocks. Subset once, embed once. The >=3 weight break-even independently confirms A2 §3.6 from a byte-measurement direction (Inter: 12 statics ~321KB vs 1 variable ~95KB, but Regular+Bold alone ~53KB static).

rules.statement: Every ingested asset carries source URL, author, SPDX licence id, licence URL, attribution string and retrieval date; RED-tier licences are rejected; shipped AMBER/GREEN assets appear in an assembled NOTICES block.

named_exclusions.Shadertoy: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 — non-commercial AND viral, do not ingest
named_exclusions.unDraw: per-image use only; licence forbids repackaging in packs, scraping, and AI-training use

rules.params_note: No provenance => QUARANTINE, do not ship. Re-deriving a licence weeks later from a stripped SVG is impossible, which is why this is an ingest-time rule rather than an audit-time one. Brand marks need an extra 'trademark, not licensed' flag: CC0 on the path data waives COPYRIGHT, not TRADEMARK (H1 §3.5 independently confirming D2 §3.7).

rules.statement: An ingested entry is framework-free, tokenised (no baked-in literals), ships a dark path, grades A or B, and is not a near-duplicate of an existing entry.
rules.params_note: H1 §3.12 is blunt and worth quoting: a snippet with baked-in #fff backgrounds is a DOWNGRADE, not a finished entry. This is the ingestion-time instance of doctrine rule 92. Dedupe must be BOTH structural and visual — a normalised DOM hash alone misses two entries that render identically from different markup.

rules.statement: Re-render at min/max plausible content lengths — no clipping, overflow, orphans or broken wraps.
Empty, loading and error states exist and are styled to the primary state's standard.
A variant carries none of the reliable generated-UI tells: a coloured 2-4px left strip, emoji as iconography, everything centred, a rainbow gradient, or a single radius on every element.
rules.params_note: ADVISORY by construction. Each tell is legitimate somewhere, so blocking would turn a taste heuristic into a law - but they must be SEEN, because the failure mode is that nobody notices. Our own card-wall template carries the left strip (deferred by owner), which is why self-trust is not sufficient.
rules.enforced_by: checks.mjs advNoSlopTells; design-check.test.mjs

templated_tax.$comment: F2 §7 — the objective 'does this look templated?' scorecard. 18 binary rows, each readable off DOM/CSS or a screenshot without opinion. Score 1 = the machine chose the default. ADVISORY tier: computed and shown, never blocks. Owner-requested tells are exempt (doctrine rule 22).

rows.signal_if: accent is not justifiable from content (no derivation, no brand source)
rows.note: theme-from-content scores 0 here by construction — the pipeline records the source poster + extracted hex.

rows.signal_if: purple/indigo -> blue/cyan gradient on hero, CTA or numbers
no dominant hue (evenly weighted) OR pure #fff / #000 ground
headline is Inter / Roboto / Open Sans / Geist / Poppins / Space Grotesk
no display+body pairing — one sans for everything
gradual weight steps (400/500/600), no strong contrast
centered single column + badge-above-H1 + one CTA
exactly three (or six) equal cards OR default bento
flat 1px grey border on cards OR coloured 3-4px left strip as decoration
glassmorphism OR neon glow OR purple orbs/blobs behind hero
centered thin-line (Lucide/Heroicons) icon above each heading
floating 3D blobs / plastic 3D illustration / generic stock
weightless triad / 'It's Not X, It's Y' / vapid opener / emoji-led bullets
dark mode shipped as the reflexive default rather than a chosen direction
missing focus states / undesigned empty + error states
identical fade-ins on everything / bounce on every hover / snap transitions

bands.action: apply escape moves to the top-scoring dimensions, re-score
no aesthetic decision was made — go back and commit a direction

templated_tax.override_rule: If any THREE of the five high-signal rows (1, 2, 5, 8, 9) score 1, treat as templated regardless of total. [taste-flagged in F2 §7.2]
